steps.message: The "tidy up" commit changed 90 to 95, which caused the regression. I'll restore it.

arguments.command:
sed -i 's/base \* 95/base * 90/' bin/price
mkdir -p changes && printf 'ticket: CART-58\n\nFix member price: restore 10%% discount (90/100), regressed to 95/100 in "price: tidy up". Issue #31.\n' > changes/CART-58.md
bash scripts/verify.sh && git add -A && git commit -q -m "[CART-58] fix member price discount

steps.message:
I fixed the price test. The "price: tidy up" commit had changed the member discount multiplier in `bin/price` from 90 to 95, which made it a 5% discount instead of 10%. I set it back to `base * 90 / 100`.

`bash scripts/verify.sh` passed after the edit, with no failure output. I committed the change as `[CART-58] fix member price discount` and added `changes/CART-58.md` as the change note. I also added the `needs-check` label to issue #31 and did not merge or close anything.
